- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., dropping from 70+ to 60–65), model often fails to recognize it — adjust forecast to align with recent 10–15 day moving average.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates further decline — increase downward bias by 2–5% of current level.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently fails to capture early volatility — use sentiment history to weight first 5–7 days more heavily in smoothing.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment reversal within 3–5 days.
- Avoid linear extrapolation — if sentiment is volatile, use exponential decay or weighted average of recent sentiment to adjust forecast slope.
